title: 4x the Room? Work-Energy Theorem Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A cycle brakes, a car brakes, a runner skids to a stop. Faster things always need more room to stop, but how much more? Aarav brakes from 4 m/s and stops in 4 m. From 8 m/s, with the same brakes, he needs 16 m: four times the room. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 5, Work, Energy and Power) for NCERT, CBSE, ISC and PUC students, plus JEE and NEET, we find the rule that predicts it: the work-energy theorem.

On a live motion notebook an 80 kg bike brakes with a steady 160 N force from 4 m/s and from 8 m/s, with a draining kinetic energy bar, a live readout, a K vs distance graph and a slow-mo replay of the force and velocity vectors. We prove K_f - K_i = W_net step by step from v^2 - u^2 = 2ad and F = ma, compare positive and negative work side by side, and show link by link why the stopping distance d = mu^2/2F grows with u squared. Two pause-and-think questions, a worked example with friction, the exam trap about net work, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.
